newsitem.title: USA: CBOT nearby soymeal ends down on funds, oil higher.
newsitem.headline: CBOT nearby soymeal ends down on funds, oil higher.

text.p: CBOT nearby soymeal futures ended down sharply Monday, under pressure from heavy commodity fund selling, CBOT floor traders said.
"The meal just tanked on the fund selling," one floor trader said.
In contrast, soyoil futures ended the day with solid gains in response to rumors of recent export business and active soyoil/soymeal spread trade, floor sources said.
On the day, E.D. and F. Man sold 500 lots July soymeal, R.J. O'Brien and Refco each sold 400 July and Rosenthal Collins sold 300 July, pit traders said.
Soyoil futures climbed on market talk that a commercial firm was an active buyer in South American vegetable oil markets last week.
U.S. exporters said there was talk that up to 60,000 tonnes of soyoil was purchased to cover spot business to either China or Iran.
CBOT soymeal settled up $0.70 to down $5.70 per ton, with July down $5.70 at $267.80 per ton. Soyoil futures closed up 0.20 to 0.60 cent per lb, with July up 0.27 at $25.09 cents per lb.
